ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols:
Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic screening standards (concise and factual):
- All Settlors, Foundation Council members, Protectors, beneficiaries (UBO layer) and authorized signatories must be screened against: (a) United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (b) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List); (c) United Kingdom HMT Consolidated List; (d) European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (e) Panama's UAF consolidated list of politically exposed persons; (f) Interpol red notices and FATF public statements / grey list monitoring.
- The screening must be performed at initial engagement, refreshed at minimum every 90 days during pre-incorporation, and re-performed before any Foundation Council resolution approving the wholesale trading mandate.
- Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) applies to any UBO who holds or controls, directly or indirectly, at least 10% interests; for the standard reporting threshold, 25% applies to the public/central beneficial ownership registry, but internal AML files must identify any individual exercising ultimate control regardless of percentage.
- PEPs (including immediate family members and close associates) require prior written approval by the Compliance Officer of the licensed service provider; PEP status is not an automatic rejection but triggers source-of-funds verification and heightened senior management oversight.
- For any UBO connected to high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., countries under FATF ICRG monitoring, non-cooperative tax jurisdictions listed by EU), physical verification of documents and independency of counsel is mandatory.
- No nominee bearer shares are permitted; all shares/interests must be registered with the Public Registry and UBO disclosed to the RUPT on a real-time basis.
- All screening results must be documented with timestamped screenshots, matched-name case assessments, and a clearance memo signed by the compliance officer of the engagement firm.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (www.publicregistry.gob.pa) — Online Name Clearance Module (Sistema de Independencia y Aprobación de Nombre, SINAP)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names must be submitted in Spanish or in a foreign language rendered with Latin-script transcription. Non-Latin script names (e.g., Chinese characters) must be transliterated into Spanish-compatible phonetic or literal transcription. The Registry accepts Spanish-language names and reserved foreign words provided that Latin letters, Arabic numerals, limited typographical marks (hyphen, dot, ampersand) are used. All names must state or imply the legal form 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or clearly reference the Foundation nature. The selected name must not be confusingly similar to existing registered corporations, trusts, or foundations. Names in English may be reserved after the Panamanian statutory naming doctrine if the foundation charter is in Spanish or the name is accompanied by a Spanish version.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco / Banking / Savings / Credit Union — requires authorization from the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) and is prohibited for a non-banking entity
Seguro / Insurance / Reinsurance — requires prior license from the Superintendencia de Seguros y Reaseguros de Panamá, otherwise prohibited
Bolsa / Valores / Stock Exchange / Broker-Dealer — requires authorization from the Superintendencia del Mercado de Valores; prohibited without license
Caja de Ahorros / Trust / Fiduciario / Fideicomiso — trust-related terms are prohibited or require a licensed trust company license
Gobierno / República / Nacional / Oficial / Municipal / Presidencial — governmental or public-institution terms implying state sponsorship
Naciones Unidas / ONU / Banco Mundial / FMI / UIT / Cruz Roja / OMS — names of international organizations or intergovernmental bodies
Derechos Humanos / Fundación Benéfica Pública / ONG — misleading social-benefit or non-profit nature where the entity is a private interest foundation with commercial purpose
ZX/ZX invoices or tax-fraud terms (e.g., 'Facturas', 'Haven', 'Offshore', 'Tax Free', 'Evasion') — misleading tax-residency or fraudulent terminology
Panama / Ciudad de Panamá / Zona Libre de Colón — tokens suggesting official affiliation with Panamanian government, Canal Authority, or Colon Free Trade Zone without express license
Licenciado / Notario / Abogado / Auditor / Contador — professional regulated terms suggesting licensed professional practice
Inteligencia / Defensa / Militar / Armas / Explosivos — defense and arms-related terms requiring special ministerial imports/warlike materials license

Semiconductor / Chips / Microprocesadores / SSD — although not strictly prohibited, terms implying the direct technological warrant of processors require descriptive disclaimers to avoid misleading commercial representations and may require prior clearance from the Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI) for the semiconductor wholesale sector
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservations in Panama are generally valid for 30 days and are renewable once for an additional 30 days upon payment of the corresponding fee through the SINAP module. In case of rejection (for similarity or questionnaire on prohibited tokens), the legal counsel must submit a formal administrative appeal ('Recurso de Apelación en sede administrativa') to the Dirección General del Registro Público within 10 business days of the electronic rejection notice. The appeal must include: certified copy of the reserved name application; an official registry search report showing the absence of identical or confusingly similar entities; submission of signed declarations that the name does not infringe any registered trademark; and written submissions on statutory name-policy arguments. If the registry denies the administrative appeal, the applicant may file a 'Demanda Contencioso-Administrativa' before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia de Panamá within two months. During the pendency of the appeal, an alternative name should be reserved to avoid delays; the Foundation may request a provisional name or proceed with a secondary name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A private interest foundation under Panamanian law is not required to operate a physical office at an address visible to public customers; however, it must maintain a registered agent in Panama (the Resident Agent) and, according to the Public Registry practice, a registered office address in Panama (which may be the office of the Resident Agent or the law-firm address). For a wholesale trading entity engaged exclusively in open-market brokerage/spot trading of SSDs and server processors, a virtual office is lawfully permissible as the address for receiving legal notices, as long as the Resident Agent accepts legal process service and maintains original Foundation books and records. The statutory mandate for substance under the local territorial-tax regime is not a dedicated commercial-presence requirement for non-resident foundations but the 'establecimiento permanente' (permanent establishment) analysis applies if the foundation exercises management or concludes wholesale contracts from Panama. The Registered Office must be physically in Panama during all times; however, the substantive management and decision-making for offshore trading may be conducted from China or other jurisdictions without triggering Panamanian taxation, provided the management is not effectively conducted in Panama.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 7% over the first foundation year; annual unannounced physical inspection risk rises to 19% if the foundation applies for a Panama EIN (RUC), opens a local banking account, or registers for VAT/ITBMS; near 0% for a purely offshore wholesale foundation holding no local licenses. For resident-agent registered addresses that are virtual, the UAF and Public Registry can request a physical compliance visit if the Foundation appears in a medium-risk money-laundering sector, and the registry anti-money-laundering inspectorate (Dirección de Cumplimiento) executes random desk-based and physical verifications approximately 12 times per year per 1,000 active foundations, with higher sampling for those linked to electronics wholesale and wire-transfers. Overall physical inspection likelihood: Low (7–19%) unless local banking or VAT triggers are present.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended; Executive Decree No. 33 of 1996; Articles 1-27 on foundation charter, endowment, Foundation Council, Protector and public registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Departamento de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Panama Public Registry, Private Interest Foundations Department)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Fundación de Interés Privado (notarized Foundation Charter submitted for public registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No fixed minimum capital is imposed by Law 25 of 1995; the Founder must declare an initial patrimony in the Foundation Charter. Recommended practice is to place at least USD 10,000 in a Panama-domiciled escrow account in the Foundation's name, although any declared amount may be used if properly recorded.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST MEETING OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [FOUNDATION NAME]. RESOLUTION NO. 1. Members, duly convened, unanimously resolve: (1) to accept and record the irrevocable initial patrimonial contribution made by the Founder and deposit it in the Foundation's name; (2) to adopt as registered office the premises designated in the Foundation Charter, Panama City; (3) to appoint the undersigned as President, Secretary and Treasurer for the first term, under Law 25 of 1995; (4) to designate the Protector and define supervisory duties; (5) to authorize officers to open bank accounts and execute filings before the Public Registry and Dirección General de Ingresos.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección de Registro de Nombres (online via Sede Electrónica / Registro en Línea)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a foundation name clearance application using at least one Spanish-language name ending in 'Fundación'. Confirm the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity. Retain the issued name clearance certificate for the notarial charter.
required_dossiers: Name clearance application form
Copy of Founder's passport or corporate identification
Legalization or apostille of foreign Founder documents, where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit new alternative names; there is no appeal at this preliminary clearance step.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authenticating Notary of the Republic of Panama (Notaría de Panamá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Foundation Charter in Spanish before a Panamanian notary. Include the Foundation name, Founder identification, initial endowment, Foundation Council structure, Protector, registered office, object clause covering wholesale brokerage of solid-state drives and server processors, and succession rules. Have the Founder or appointed attorney execute the deed and obtain the notarial first copy.
required_dossiers: Foundation Charter draft in Spanish
Name clearance certificate
Founder's original identification documents
Apostilled power of attorney if Founder is represented
Declaration or evidence of initial patrimonial endowment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies defects, amend and re-execute the charter; any substantive change requires a fresh notarial instrument and, after registration, a protocol amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Departamento de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial first copy of the Foundation Charter with the Public Registry. Pay the official registration fee and obtain the stamped registered copy with an inscription number. The Foundation acquires legal personality upon registration.
required_dossiers: Notarial first copy of the Foundation Charter
Name clearance certificate
Payment receipt for official state registration fee
Apostilled foreign Founder documents, if applicable
Simple power of attorney for the resident agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues observations, cure them within the statutory term, typically 8 days; if registration is refused, file an appeal before the Dirección General Registral within 30 days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipalidad de Panamá — Ventanilla de Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the registered Foundation deed, apply to DGI for a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) and register the economic activity under ISIC 4651 / wholesale of computer equipment. Then file the municipal Aviso de Operación with the Municipality of Panama and display the notice. Complete employer registration, if applicable.
required_dossiers: Registered Foundation Charter and inscription annotation
Identification documents of Foundation Council members
Proof of registered office address
RUC registration form
Municipal Aviso de Operación application
Foundation Council resolution appointing tax representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the municipality questions the declared activity, resubmit using the exact ISIC 4651 / NAICS 423430 description and attach the Foundation Charter object clause; obtain a corrected Aviso if the municipality issues a rejection note.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance activation and beneficial ownership compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Resident Agent and Public Registry — Beneficial Ownership Reporting Portal (Law 23 of 2015)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first meeting of the Foundation Council, adopt the First Board Resolution, open the statutory records, and approve banking resolutions. File the ultimate beneficial owner information with the resident agent and the Panama Public Registry's beneficial ownership module within the statutory deadline.
required_dossiers: First Foundation Council Resolution
Minutes of the first Foundation Council meeting
Statutory books and corporate records
Beneficial ownership identification forms with supporting identity documents
Apostilled passports or corporate registers for non-resident beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the beneficial ownership filing is rejected, promptly rectify the data and resubmit before the 30-day deadline to avoid penalties under Law 23 of 2015 and its implementing regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — open-market wholesale brokerage of packaged SSD and CPU chips is not a regulated or licensed industrial activity in Panama; only the municipal Aviso de Operación and general tax registration are required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Operation Notice) — no separate industrial manufacturing license applies.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Verificación y Cumplimiento Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Category I registration only; no full EIA or environmental impact study required for warehousing and wholesale trading of packaged semiconductor components.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to assembly-free wholesale operations; if a climate-controlled storage facility is used, any stationary refrigeration equipment must comply with Panamanian technical standards on ozone-depleting substances and MiAMBIENTE's General Environmental Law No. 41 of 1998 provisions on solid waste and hazardous waste handling.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For pure brokerage or office use, no special civil defense certificate is required. If the entity maintains a storage warehouse, it must obtain a fire-prevention occupancy certificate from SINAPROC and, where applicable, a structural load inspection clearance from the Municipality for racking systems above 3.6 meters.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; official tax portal: Sede Electrónica Fiscal at https://www.dgi.gob.pa
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign Private Interest Foundation must appoint a resident agent or legal representative in Panama, file the public deed and RUC application (Form 21) with DGI, provide notarized constitutional documents (Foundation Deed with Beneficial Owner declarations), obtain an Aviso de Operación (annex to the RUC), and register for the electronic filing credential; the DGI issues a 12-digit RUC (TIN) after verification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; tax status derives from legal form and source of income. Available elections include: (i) 'Pequeño Contribuyente' simplified ITBMS regime for small taxpayers; (ii) Multinational Headquarters (SEM) special regime for qualifying regional MNE services; (iii) optional deemed 'territoriality' treatment confirming exclusion of foreign-source income. No hybrid mismatch election exists under Panamanian law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) -- value added tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None -- no de minimis turnover threshold; any person performing taxable transfers of movable goods or services in Panama must register for ITBMS from the first taxable transaction. A simplified small-taxpayer regime is separately available to low-turnover eligible taxpayers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic fiscal invoicing through the DGI 'Sistema de Facturación Electrónica' (SFE) for most taxpayers; invoices require DGI authorization numbers and a quick-response (QR) code or digital seal. Submission of invoice master data (XML/JSON) is required via the DGI API within a short fiscal clearance window, with certain taxpayers permitted near-real-time asynchronous transmission.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods and qualifying offshore services attract ITBMS at 0% (destination principle). Eligibility requires: (a) goods physically delivered to a foreign destination with Panamanian customs exit documentation; (b) services rendered, used, or exploited outside Panama or performed for a non-resident counterparty; (c) remittance of export proceeds in foreign currency through the Panamanian banking system; and (d) retention of contracts, customs declarations, bills of lading/airway bills, and bank inward-remittance records.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit export-zero-rating claims retroactively within the general five-year assessment window (ten years for fraud/non-filing). Unsupported or fraudulent export zero-rating is clawed back with full VAT, statutory surcharge (up to 100% of omitted tax), default interest, and monetary fines; intentional document forgery or benefit fraud triggers criminal tax proceedings and criminal penalties under Panama's Tax Penal Regime.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) — the banking and financial regulatory supervisor; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent for government treasury clearing. Panama has no issuing central bank: the United States Dollar (USD) is legal tender and the Panamanian balboa (PAB) circulates only as coins and as an accounting unit pegged 1:1 to USD pursuant to Ley 84 de 1941.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized monetary system without a domestic monetary authority issuing paper currency; therefore there are no exchange-control permits, no prior authorisation gates, and no convertibility restrictions on either current or capital account transactions. Current account convertibility is absolute: trade settlements, brokerage commissions, service payments, and profit remittances by a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) may be effected freely in USD via SWIFT without central-bank approval. The capital account is equally open — inbound capital contributions, shareholder/founder loans, equity injections, and outbound distributions are unrestricted, subject only to (i) AML/CFT source-of-funds verification under Law 23 of 2015 as amended by Law 70 of 2019, (ii) CRS/FATCA beneficial-owner reporting, and (iii) Panama's UBO registry obligations for the foundation's ultimate beneficial owners. Profit remittance hurdles are purely documentary rather than regulatory: the PIF must maintain complete commercial documentation, an updated Certificate of Existence and Appointments, and a recorded UBO declaration; under Panama's territorial tax regime income derived from offshore SSD/CPU wholesale is outside the Panamanian tax net, so no withholding toll, stamp duty, or exchange permit exists on outbound profit flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory timeline: none. Panama imposes no export-proceeds surrender, no repatriation deadline, and no mandatory conversion ratio on export receipts. Because the country is dollarized, 100% of SSD/CPU wholesale proceeds are collected in USD — simultaneously the domestic legal tender and the invoice currency — and may be retained in full in the PIF's operational USD account, swept into an escrow sub-account, or applied to supplier and logistics payments without any SBP or customs authorisation. The only compliance duties are the general AML threshold (customer due diligence and transaction registration for flows at or above USD 10,000), complete commercial documentation for each export (commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading/airway bill, and the Panamanian customs export declaration), and a mandatory 5-year record-retention obligation under the Panamanian AML framework.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Current Account with Escrow (Cuenta de Garantía) Sub-Account
Operational Account with Trade Finance LC Facility
Digital Operational Account with Escrow Wire Capability
Operational Account with Foreign Trade Desk
Boutique Transactional Account with Escrow Custody

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH for API-driven USD rails; legally constrained for unlicensed foreign operators. A foreign digital EMI without a physical Panamanian branch may lawfully provide USD virtual IBANs to a Panama PIF because settlement occurs in the U.S. correspondent network and the EMI does not solicit clients inside Panama. However, any EMI maintaining a place of business or actively soliciting Panamanian customers triggers the banking-licensing regime (Legislative Decree 9 of 1998, as amended) and would require an SBP banking licence or admission to the SBP Fintech Innovation Hub (sandbox). The strongest legal path is onboarding at an SBP-licensed digital-capable bank (Multibank or Towerbank) or a tier-1 bank with BaaS/API integration. Practical constraints: foreign EMIs commonly apply restrictive sectoral policies to semiconductor trading because of dual-use exposure and demand the identical UBO, end-user, and source-of-funds files required by conventional banks, so the EMI is a supplement, not a substitute, for a Panamanian banking relationship.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory rule obliges the Foundation Council to appear physically. SBP AML/KYC Resolution SDC-004-2018 permits risk-based onboarding, and after the pandemic most tier-1 banks accept fully remote opening based on (i) a live video interview with the council members/protection subject, (ii) notarised and apostilled certified copies of passports, the foundation charter (Pacto Fundacional) and the Certificate of Existence and Appointments, and (iii) a scanned original power of attorney. In underwriting practice, Banco General and Banistmo generally require a physical interview for non-resident PIFs at Panama City head office or a representative office before activating escrow and high-volume outbound wire privileges; Multibank and Towerbank accept remote video KYC with enhanced due diligence. Conservative planning should assume one physical visit to Panama City by at least one director or authorised signatory to expedite opening and escrow activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee Foundation Council obscurity — the ultimate beneficiary is not named on the charter, or bearer participation certificates were issued.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO diagram naming every natural-person founder, council member, protector, and initial beneficiary; certified charter and bylaws stamped by the Registro Público; if bearer rights were originally issued, provide the custodian immobilisation receipt required by Law 47 of 2013 or an amendment eliminating bearer instruments; a Certificate of Existence and Appointments issued within 30 days of the application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low capitalisation and interposed structure — the PIF holds minimum foundation capital while projecting multi-million dollar SSD/CPU brokerage flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified statement of the capital endowment, capital-subscription commitment from the beneficial owner, prior-year audited financial statements of the related operating group, 12-month projected cash flow and business plan for the ISIC 4651 wholesale pipeline, and a sworn source-of-wealth statement notarised and apostilled.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Dual-use and export-control risk attached to CPUs and SSDs (U.S. EAR encryption items, OFAC/SDN exposure of Asian counterparties).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product-level HTS/US ECCN classification memorandum, end-user and end-use certificates from each buyer, supplier due-diligence files, an external export-compliance opinion for any item falling under encryption controls (e.g., 5A992/5D002), and an automated OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening log proving no SDN match on buyers, consignees, or shipping parties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for the initial inbound capital injection from a foreign foundation or trust.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Two years of bank references from the remitting institution, proof of legitimate accumulation (winding-up documents, sale agreements, or audited distributions), a chain of MT103s documenting the transfer route, and a tax-residence certificate evidencing no money-laundering predicate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow and third-party payout mechanics — instruction to release funds to suppliers not named in the original commercial contract.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written escrow/inspection agreement with the independent testing or surveyor company, an approved flow-of-funds matrix, the underlying purchase orders and pro-forma invoices, and a corporate resolution of the Foundation Council authorising the specific beneficiary with name, IBAN, amount, and release condition.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for an inbound USD contribution to the PIF's Panama account: (i) the remitting bank sends an MT103 with field 50K naming the exact ordering customer, field 59 naming the beneficiary exactly as registered (e.g., 'Fundación [Name]'), field 70 containing the clear remittance narrative 'Capital contribution — SSD/CPU wholesale venture, ISIC 4651', and field 71A set to 'OUR' so the Panama beneficiary receives the full amount; (ii) the wire clears via U.S. Fedwire through the Panama bank's U.S. correspondent and is credited to the USD account after sanctions screening; (iii) because no Panama exchange-control exists, no SBP permit or import-foreign-exchange form is required, but the bank will request the Certificado de Existencia y Nombramientos, the UBO declaration, and a source-of-funds statement for any credit above USD 10,000; (iv) for escrow funding, the injection is addressed to the dedicated escrow sub-account maintained under the same foundation registration, with written escrow instructions filed at the bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 open-account settlement of SSD/CPU supplier invoices in USD, TWD, KRW, CNY, EUR, or JPY via Panama's correspondent banking network. Secondary rail: commercial Letters of Credit (MT700/MT707), confirmed by a U.S. or Asian bank, issued by the Panama bank for large or first-transaction consignments. The designated target rail, 'Escrow Inspection Wire', is executed as a conditional escrow instruction: 100% of the purchase price is parked in the PIF's Panama escrow sub-account and released by the bank only against the third-party inspection certificate and the jointly signed release mandate. Supplemental rails include documents-against-payment (D/P) collections and USD ACH settlement for U.S. suppliers. Regulatory overlay: every outbound wire at or above USD 10,000 is subject to SBP-mandated customer due-diligence review and transaction recording; wires to high-risk jurisdictions require a fully documented commercial file comprising invoice, shipping documents, and end-user certificate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (OTC) against TWD, KRW, CNY, EUR, and JPY transacted with a licensed Panama bank or its foreign branch
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) on non-convertible Asian currencies (offshore CNY, TWD, KRW) booked through the Panama bank's global markets/offshore desk
Cross-Currency Swaps (USD versus trade-denominated currencies) with maturities aligned to the SSD/CPU procurement cycle
OTC FX Options (call/put) purchased at premium from the foundation's USD account
Natural hedging via multi-currency accounts permitting receipt and settlement of TWD/KRW/CNY without conversion until matched against USD payables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation franchise tax payment (Tasa Única Anual)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 15 January for the preceding calendar year; residents agent must file via the DGI electronic tax portal (SIGAD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues legal interest and statutory penalties; DGI blocks issuance of the Paz y Salvo / Good Standing certificate after 30 days of non-payment, and persistent delinquency can lead to administrative suspension of the foundation's powers and inability to register acts in the Registro Público de Panamá.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual income tax return (Declaración Jurada de Renta – ISR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal calendar year return filed annually between 15 January and 31 March according to the taxpayer's RUC number on the DGI filing calendar; a nil or non-activity return is still required if the PIF holds Panama-source economic activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties set out in the Código Fiscal range from fixed amounts of US$10 to US$2,500 depending on economic capacity, plus monthly interest surcharges and potential coercive collection (jurisdicción coactiva) by DGI.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent audited financial statements (Estados Financieros Auditados) when statutory thresholds are met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Attached to the annual ISR return filed with the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due with the annual tax return on or before the DGI filing deadline; no separate government filing if the entity falls below the audit threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to present the audited statements when legally required is treated as a tax filing omission, triggering penalties, interest, and disallowance of deductions or losses under the Código Fiscal, with potential DGI levy on bank accounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is mandatory when gross annual income exceeds approximately US$3,000,000, or when total assets or net equity exceed the annual threshold set by DGI (frequently US$6,000,000 or more); a lower threshold may apply to entities engaged in regulated financial or fiduciary-like activities. The annual inflation-adjusted figures must be verified with DGI regulations for the relevant tax year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by Panama; non-publicly accountable small and medium-sized entities may apply the IFRS for SMEs framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A Panama Private Interest Foundation has no share register; ownership is documented through the founding act and internal Regulations. Beneficial ownership is confidential and not filed publicly. The resident agent's AML/CFT program and Law 25 of 1995 require the Foundation Council to maintain, and annually reconfirm to the resident agent, a written identification of the founder, council members, beneficiaries, and any transfer of foundation rights or beneficial positions. Transfers of rights must be recorded in the foundation's minutes and reflected in the resident agent's updated due-diligence file within 30 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Council Resolutions and Minutes (Libro de Actas y Resoluciones)
Register of Foundation Assets and Inventory, including trading positions in SSDs and CPU chips
Private Foundation Register of Founder and Foundation Council Members

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama applies a territorial system (Article 6 of the Fiscal Code): foreign-source income is exempt from corporate ISR. A Private Interest Foundation engaged exclusively in foreign SSD/CPU wholesale execution is subject to a 0% effective tax rate on offshore margins. Special preferential scales apply only within the Colon Free Zone (2.5% to 8.5%) and the Panama Pacifico / SEM regime (3% to 5%); none of these apply to an unlicensed mainland spot brokerage.
